subject: ordinal,relation_type
justification: ordinal is a positional bookkeeping index inside one page's parse (builder lines 488, 500) and relation_type has 3 values; neither identifies anything. The FD holds only because every page on this site emits the same templated head, so the nth resource reference is the same tag on all 422 pages. One page with an extra stylesheet breaks it.

subject: tag
justification: The builder explicitly permits several attributes per tag - ASSET_ATTRS maps img to ('src','srcset'), video to ('src','poster'), use to ('href','xlink:href'), plus synthesised 'style:url' and 'url' attrs (builder lines 46-56, 240, 457). The FD holds only because this mirror happens to use src on img/script and href on link and nothing else (measured 4 tags, 3 attrs, one attr per tag). A single srcset or inline style breaks it; an HTML tag does not own the attribute a page referenced it through.

subject: target_stable_id -> attr
justification: attr and tag describe the element that carries the link -- href/link, src/img, src/script -- so they are properties of the edge, not of the target it points at. Across 17422 edges over 1396 targets each target happens to be referenced the same way, which a single page linking one URL both as an anchor and as an image would end.

subject: target_stable_id -> target_url
justification: the stable_id is a slug of the url: `?mr=MR0857454` becomes `-mr-mr0857454`. The transformation discards characters, so two urls differing only in what it flattens produce one stable_id, and recovering the url from it is not possible in general. It holds here because no such pair was crawled.

subject: target_url -> target_stable_id

subject: text
justification: The pair owns the derived label; the label does not own its components. text is the formatted concatenation written at builder line 673, so it re-yields target_url only by string containment with the direction of derivation reversed, and it is near-unique (16636 distinct over 17422 rows). tag and attr ride on exactly the target->tag coincidence rejected under target_stable_id. Treating this as real would license normalising edges around its own display string.

subject: model
value: One row is one individual reference occurrence: the n-th outgoing reference of a given relation type on one crawled page, pointing at one link or asset target.
justification: `_edge_row` (662-688) is called once per ref (573, 633), so a row is one reference occurrence, and its `stable_id` (declared PRIMARY KEY, 414) is hashed from `{source}:{relation_type}:{target}:{ordinal}` (671). `ordinal` is `enumerate(parser.links)` for links_to and `enumerate(parser.resources)` for references_asset/references_svg (488-512): two disjoint index spaces, each index producing exactly one row, with relation_type separating the spaces. Hence (source, relation_type, ordinal) identifies a row by construction and determines the target — verified: 0 collisions over 17,422 rows, while (source, ordinal) alone collides 6,837 times, exactly as the two enumerations predict. `source_url` and `source_stable_id` are bijective via `_page_stable_id` (150-155; 422/422 distinct page urls), so both spellings are the same key. The other nine observed combinations are artifacts: `attr` and `tag` are '' on every links_to edge (681-683); the target_stable_id/target_url variants drop relation_type and survive only because link ids and asset ids never share a subdomain prefix; `ordinal,text` rides on text = source_url+relation_type+target_url (673). Scope per-build (405-407).

Hence (source, relation_type, ordinal) identifies a row by construction and determines the target — verified: 0 collisions over 17,422 rows, while (source, ordinal) alone collides 6,837 times, exactly as the two enumerations predict. `source_url` and `source_stable_id` are bijective via `_page_stable_id` (150-155; 422/422 distinct page urls), so both spellings are the same key. The other nine observed combinations are artifacts: `attr` and `tag` are '' on every links_to edge (681-683); the target_stable_id/target_url variants drop relation_type and survive only because link ids and asset ids never share a subdomain prefix; `ordinal,text` rides on text = source_url+relation_type+target_url (673). subject: model
value: One row is one SVG graphic in the walk: either one inline <svg> occurrence inside a crawled page, or one external .svg asset referenced by the pages.
justification: `svgs` is a union of two branches. Inline (513-525): one row per `<svg` occurrence, with `url = record.url` and page_url/page_stable_id set, so N inline SVGs on one page share url, page_url and page_stable_id and carry no local_path, relative_path, sha256 or asset_stable_id.
